title: SEM services in Singapore: what is included and what it costs

rm_title: SEM services in Singapore: scope, CPCs & costs
rm_desc: SEM services in Singapore: what is included, real CPC benchmarks by industry and how management pricing works, from a flat retainer. See the breakdown.
content: SEM, search engine marketing, is paid placement on search results. In Singapore it is the fastest lever most businesses have, and also one of the easiest budgets to waste. Here is what proper Singapore SEM services include, what clicks actually cost here, and how management pricing works.
What Singapore SEM services actually include

Running ads is the smallest part. A serious SEM service covers intent-led campaign structure across branded, generic, competitor and category keywords; ongoing search-term mining and negative keyword management, which is where wasted spend hides; smart bidding strategy and bid testing; ad copy and asset testing; audience layering and remarketing; and for e-commerce, Shopping and Performance Max. For app businesses, Apple Search Ads and Google App campaigns belong in scope too. If a proposal only mentions "campaign setup and monthly reporting", you are looking at a dashboard.

Singapore is a small, intensely contested market, and the CPCs behind SEM services reflect it. From the keyword data we work with daily: "seo agency singapore" runs around US$10 per click, "digital marketing agency singapore" over US$11, and "sem agency singapore" close to US$14. At the extreme end, financial services keywords in Singapore run roughly S$5–18 per click. At those rates, structure and negatives decide whether a budget produces pipeline or noise. Treat every figure here as an average with a wide spread: actual CPCs move with match types, quality scores, seasonality and who else decided to bid this quarter. Google's own Quality Score documentation is worth reading before you argue with an account manager about why your CPC sits where it does.
What a proposal should specify in writing

Before signing for any SEM services, ask for the account structure: campaign types, how negatives are reviewed and how often, who owns bid strategy changes, and what a month-one versus month-three report looks like. A vague answer here predicts a vague account later. The agencies worth hiring can show you a real, anonymised account structure from an existing client in the first call; the ones who cannot are selling you the pitch.

SEM services are priced under three common models: percentage of ad spend (typically 10–20%), flat monthly retainer, or hybrid. Each has a failure mode: percentage models reward spending more and flat retainers can reward doing less. The safeguard is transparency. We work on flat retainers, paid media management from SGD 2,200 a month, with media billed at net cost and 0% markup, platform invoices attached to every recharge. Whatever model you choose, insist on seeing platform billing directly. Media margin hidden inside "management" is a common trick.

The better question is sequencing. SEM buys visibility today; SEO compounds it over quarters. Whether that sequencing suits you depends on unit economics: at S$10+ per click, thin margins can make SEM a treadmill, while high-LTV businesses can afford it indefinitely. Most Singapore businesses we work with run SEM immediately while SEO builds underneath, then rebalance as organic takes share, and the rebalancing point is a margin decision. We have written a full comparison in SEO vs SEM, and the organic half of the picture is set out on our SEO service page.
How to read a proposal for SEM services line by line

A proposal for SEM services should read like a work plan. Take it apart line by line and ask what each item actually produces. "Keyword research" should name the themes and the intent you will target. "Ad copy" should say how many variants run and how often they are reviewed. "Optimisation" on its own means nothing; it needs a cadence and an owner.
• Conversion tracking is set up and tested before any budget is spent, with the primary conversion defined as a lead or a sale.
• Search term review has a schedule and an owner. Ask how often queries are checked and who adds the negatives, because that is where wasted spend is found.
• Reporting shows cost per qualified lead or acquisition, with clicks and impressions below it, in plain words.
• The ad account is in your name, with the agency added as a user. If they own the account, you cannot take your history with you.
• The management fee and the media budget are separate lines, and the media is billed at net cost.
The landing page is half of any SEM services result

You can buy the best clicks in Singapore and still lose them on arrival. Paid traffic is unforgiving: every visitor was paid for, so a slow page, a confusing form or a message that does not match the ad turns budget into noise. A good set of SEM services therefore looks past the ad account and asks about the page the ad points to.

The checks are practical. Does the headline repeat what the searcher typed? Is the next step obvious without scrolling on a phone? Does the form ask for only what you need to follow up? For many Singapore businesses, a click-to-call or WhatsApp button converts better than a long form, so test it. If an agency will not touch the landing page, or you cannot change it, tell them before the campaign starts, because that limit will cap the result.

You do not need to be a specialist to spot a healthy account in a screen-share. Branded and generic searches should sit in separate campaigns so you can see what each is really worth. The search term report should show negative keywords being added regularly. Conversions should be counted once, from a source you trust, and budget should follow the campaigns that produce them. If an agency running your SEM services cannot show these three things in the first call, the account is probably being run on defaults.
Questions about SEM services in Singapore
Is SEM the same as Google Ads?

Google Ads is the main platform, so the two are often used as one word. SEM is the wider practice of buying search visibility, and it can include Microsoft Advertising and other search platforms, though Google carries most of the volume in Singapore.
How long before we know it is working?

You will see clicks and enquiries within days, but a fair judgement takes longer. Automated bidding needs a steady flow of conversions to learn, so give each change a few weeks before drawing conclusions, and judge by cost per qualified lead over that period rather than by any single day.

Enough to buy a meaningful number of conversions each month at your real cost per click. If the budget only buys a handful of clicks, you will not learn anything useful. Work backwards from the number of leads you need and what a qualified lead is worth to you, and let that set the budget.

Judge SEM services on cost per qualified lead or acquisition and on revenue, never on impressions or clicks. When we restructured paid search for a premium B2B corporate-gifting brand, conversion rates rose 50% and qualified leads grew 150% with no extra budget: the money moved from wasted queries to buying ones. Gains that size are what fixing a poorly structured account looks like. A well-run account improves in single digits, and anyone promising 150% on top of good work is promising arithmetic that does not exist. The job is the same either way: move money from waste to buyers. If you want your account held to that standard, here is how we run paid search.
